question: A Treasury quote is 99.16 in 32nds notation. What decimal price does it represent?
source: Treasury price quotes can use a whole-number part followed by a fractional part. In this case the quoted fractional part is 16 thirty-seconds.

question: A Treasury quote is 101.08+ in 32nds notation. What decimal price does it represent?
source: Treasury price quotes can use a plus suffix to denote an extra half of one thirty-second. The quote 101.08+ has whole part 101 and fractional part 8.5 thirty-seconds.
